title: Are PRNGs used for weight initialization during model training?
question: Are PRNGs (pseudorandom number generators) used for weight initialization during model training? If yes, do they use standard algorithms like WELL, Mersenne Twister or Xorshift, or they use specialized algorithms?
answer: Yes, they are. Weight initialization just draws from the framework's default random number generator, so the answer depends on which framework and device you use. In PyTorch the default CPU generator is Mersenne Twister (mt19937), while on CUDA it is Philox (Philox4x32-10). JAX uses Threefry by default, and TensorFlow's stateless random ops use Philox or Threefry. The exact generator hardly affects training quality, since any decent PRNG gives samples that are statistically fine for initialization. What matters more is the seed: fixing it (torch.manual_seed, jax.random.PRNGKey) is what makes an initialization reproducible, and results can still differ between CPU and GPU because they use different generators.
